summary: Updates RFC 3777 to clarify whether sitting members of IETF leadership bodies, including the IAOC and ex officio members and liaisons, can volunteer for the nominating committee. It was replaced by RFC 7437.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 6859 clarifies which IETF leadership members cannot volunteer as voting members of the Nominating Committee. It includes ex officio members of four named bodies and does not exclude liaisons; RFC 7437 later obsoleted the update.

subtitle: Clarifies which IETF leadership members may serve on the NomCom.

tldr.problem: RFC 3777 did not cover the IAOC and left unclear whether ex officio members and liaisons counted as sitting members for NomCom eligibility.
tldr.mechanism: The update excludes members, including ex officio members, of the Internet Society Board of Trustees, IAB, IESG, and IAOC from volunteering as voting NomCom members; liaisons are not excluded.
tldr.outcome: RFC 6859 updates RFC 3777 and was obsoleted by RFC 7437.

facts.label: Bodies named
facts.value: Internet Society Board of Trustees, IAB, IESG, IAOC

today: RFC 6859 is a Best Current Practice, updates RFC 3777, and was obsoleted by RFC 7437.

sections.title: Why the Eligibility Rule Needed Clarity
sections.content:
RFC 3777 said that sitting IAB and IESG members may not volunteer for the NomCom. The IAOC was formed later, and some IAOC members are selected by the NomCom, but RFC 3777 did not include it. The older rule also left unclear whether ex officio members and liaisons counted as sitting members.

The stated purpose is to avoid having bodies select their own successors while allowing experienced people from the wider community to participate.
sections.plainLanguage: The existing rule named two leadership bodies but not the IAOC, and it was unclear who counted as a member. This update defines the groups covered.

sections.title: Who May Not Volunteer as a Voting Member
sections.content:
Any person serving on the Internet Society Board of Trustees, the IAB, the IESG, or the IAOC may not volunteer as a voting member of the NomCom. This includes people serving on those bodies in ex officio positions. Liaisons to those bodies from other organizations are not excluded by this rule.

The RFC says this restriction does not extend to working group chairs, IRTF research group chairs, directorate and review-team members, or members of other advisory bodies.
sections.plainLanguage: Current members of the four named bodies, including ex officio members, cannot be voting NomCom volunteers. Liaisons and people in other roles are not barred by this rule.

sections.title: Security and Status
sections.content: The RFC describes itself as procedural and unrelated to security. It updates RFC 3777 and was later obsoleted by RFC 7437.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo changes a committee eligibility procedure, not a security protocol. RFC 7437 later replaced it.
